title: Future 1
note: NEW 2026-09-05, James dropdowns (interactive session): B1 future consolidation plus future time clauses. Amends the 2026-09-01 B1-PLAN lock 'future forms consolidation is not a unit'; takes the 60th path slot freed when b1_present_perfect_continuous was retired 2026-09-04. Scope: will (decide now / offer / promise) vs going to (plan / evidence) vs present continuous (arrangement) vs present simple (timetable), plus the NEW ground: when / until / as soon as / before / after + present simple (the 'When I will arrive' calque). C57 card 1 recaps a2_will_going_to and a2_arrangements. C29 timeline on card 0, now as centre line, future forms to the right. B4 the unit's own errors are chips (will + infinitive-with-to, bare present for decide-now, will inside a time clause, missing be before going to). B13/B1: on arrangement and prediction items where the sibling future form is real English, distractors are form errors, never the sibling; sibling chips appear only on stems whose job forces the form (A2 precedent). A0: 'has a meeting' twins and word-order variants in accepts. A3 licensed deliberately in time-clause items: the Czech perfective future in the subordinate clause is exactly what English renders as present simple - that IS the teaching point. E7 use_mode correct; E9/G4 every wrong is clearly not English. Kept clear of b1_modals_speculation (might/may/could predictions - F2) and of shall (untaught). Lint 2026-09-05: 0 EXACT. Standing CANDIDATEs, do not re-open: 6x A4 the-demands are all English-forced known referents (our office windows, the rain, the result, the way home, the tickets, the hotel/the dates) - the four items where Czech carried a demonstrative naturally already got one (ten film, Tu barvu, s tim novym manazerem, ten zapas); 21x F3-above-A1 is the recorded lint-downgraded class.

cards.title: Future 1
points: You know three ways to talk about the future. The job now is **choosing**.

table.caption: the forms
rows: am / is / are + going to + verb

cards.title: You already know
points: All of this is from A2. New here: choosing between them, and time clauses.

table.caption: jobs
rows: It's hot. I **will** open the window.
We have tickets. We are **going to** watch a film.
Look at the sky. It is **going to** rain.
I**'m meeting** Petra at ten tomorrow.

cards.title: Choosing the form
points: Czech *budu / -u* covers all of these. English asks **when** the decision happened.

table.caption: choose
rows: Arranged with a person, time and place fixed
am / is / are + **-ing** — I'm meeting Jana at ten.

examples.en: I**'m playing** tennis with Martin on Friday.
examples.cz: V pátek hraju s Martinem tenis. (domluvené)

cards.title: Predictions
points: Czech **bude** covers both. English asks: your opinion, or evidence you can see?

table.caption: predict
rows: Evidence now — you can see it
**going to** — Look at those clouds. It's **going to** rain.
**going to** — Be careful! You're **going to** break that glass.

cards.title: When I arrive — time clauses
points: Czech puts the future in **both** parts. English puts it in **one**.

tables.caption: not
rows: ~~When I will arrive, I'll call you.~~

examples.en: I'll call you when I **get** home.
*As soon as* the meeting finishes, I'll send you a message.
examples.cz: Jakmile schůzka skončí, pošlu ti zprávu.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Czech says the future with the verb ending. English needs the **word**.

rows: ~~When I will arrive, I'll call you.~~
She is **going to** study in Vienna.

items.en: I'll call you when I get home from work.
items.cz: Zavolám ti, až přijdu domů z práce.
items.gap: I'll call you when I ____ home from work. (get)
accepts: I'll call you when I get home from work.
I will call you when I get home from work.
When I get home from work, I'll call you.
When I get home from work, I will call you.
items.wrong: I'll call you when I will get home from work.
items.explanation: After **when** in a future sentence: present simple — **get**, never ~~will get~~.
items.explanation_cz: Po **when** ve větě o budoucnosti: přítomný čas — **get**, nikdy ~~will get~~.

items.en: We'll order some food as soon as you arrive.
items.cz: Objednáme jídlo, jakmile přijedeš.
items.gap: We'll order some food as soon as you ____. (arrive)
accepts: We'll order some food as soon as you arrive.
We will order some food as soon as you arrive.
We'll order food as soon as you arrive.
We will order food as soon as you arrive.
As soon as you arrive, we'll order some food.
As soon as you arrive, we will order some food.
As soon as you arrive, we'll order food.
As soon as you arrive, we will order food.
items.wrong: We'll order some food as soon as you will arrive.
items.explanation: **as soon as** works like *when*: present simple — **arrive**.
items.explanation_cz: **as soon as** funguje jako *when*: přítomný čas — **arrive**.

items.en: She will move to Brno when she finds a new job.
items.cz: Až si najde novou práci, přestěhuje se do Brna.
items.gap: She will move to Brno when she ____ a new job. (find)
accepts: She will move to Brno when she finds a new job.
She'll move to Brno when she finds a new job.
When she finds a new job, she will move to Brno.
When she finds a new job, she'll move to Brno.
items.wrong: She will move to Brno when she will find a new job.
items.explanation: Present simple in the *when* clause — and third person: **finds**.
items.explanation_cz: Přítomný čas ve větě s *when* — a třetí osoba: **finds**.

items.en: We'll close the windows before we leave the office.
items.cz: Než odejdeme z kanceláře, zavřeme okna.
items.gap: We'll close the windows before we ____ the office. (leave)
accepts: We'll close the windows before we leave the office.
We will close the windows before we leave the office.
Before we leave the office, we'll close the windows.
Before we leave the office, we will close the windows.
items.wrong: We'll close the windows before we will leave the office.
items.explanation: **before** takes present simple too: before we **leave**.
items.explanation_cz: **before** má taky přítomný čas: before we **leave**.

items.en: After the film ends, we'll get some dinner.
items.cz: Až ten film skončí, dáme si večeři.
items.gap: After the film ____, we'll get some dinner. (end)
accepts: After the film ends, we'll get some dinner.
After the film ends, we will get some dinner.
We'll get some dinner after the film ends.
We will get some dinner after the film ends.
After the film ends, we'll have dinner.
After the film ends, we will have dinner.
We'll have dinner after the film ends.
We will have dinner after the film ends.
items.wrong: After the film will end, we'll get some dinner.
items.explanation: **after** + present simple: the film **ends**. The future sits in *we'll go*.
items.explanation_cz: **after** + přítomný čas: the film **ends**. Budoucnost nese *we'll go*.

items.en: I'll wait here until the rain stops.
items.cz: Počkám tady, dokud déšť nepřestane.
items.gap: I'll wait here until the rain ____. (stop)
accepts: I'll wait here until the rain stops.
I will wait here until the rain stops.
Until the rain stops, I'll wait here.
Until the rain stops, I will wait here.
items.wrong: I'll wait here until the rain will stop.
items.explanation: Czech says *dokud NEpřestane*. English is positive after **until**: until it **stops**.
items.explanation_cz: Čeština říká *dokud NEpřestane*. Angličtina má po **until** kladné sloveso: until it **stops**.

items.en: When I'm in Prague next week, I will visit you.
items.cz: Až budu příští týden v Praze, navštívím tě.
items.gap: When I'm in Prague next week, I ____ you. (visit)
accepts: When I'm in Prague next week, I will visit you.
When I'm in Prague next week, I'll visit you.
When I am in Prague next week, I will visit you.
When I am in Prague next week, I'll visit you.
I will visit you when I'm in Prague next week.
I'll visit you when I'm in Prague next week.
I will visit you when I am in Prague next week.
I'll visit you when I am in Prague next week.
items.wrong: When I'm in Prague next week, I visit you.
items.explanation: The future goes in the **main** clause: **will visit**. The *when* clause already did its job.
items.explanation_cz: Budoucnost patří do **hlavní** věty: **will visit**. Věta s *when* už své udělala.

items.en: As soon as the meeting finishes, I will send you a message.
items.cz: Jakmile schůzka skončí, pošlu ti zprávu.
items.gap: As soon as the meeting finishes, I ____ you a message. (send)
accepts: As soon as the meeting finishes, I will send you a message.
As soon as the meeting finishes, I'll send you a message.
I will send you a message as soon as the meeting finishes.
I'll send you a message as soon as the meeting finishes.
items.wrong: As soon as the meeting will finish, I'll send you a message.
items.explanation: Main clause carries the future: **will send**. *Finishes* stays present simple.
items.explanation_cz: Hlavní věta nese budoucnost: **will send**. *Finishes* zůstává v přítomném čase.

items.en: I won't start the meeting until everyone is here.
items.cz: Nezačnu schůzku, dokud tu nebudou všichni.
items.gap: I ____ the meeting until everyone is here. (not start)
accepts: I won't start the meeting until everyone is here.
I will not start the meeting until everyone is here.
items.wrong: I won't start the meeting until everyone will be here.
items.explanation: Negative future in the main clause: **won't start**. After *until*: present simple *is*.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná budoucnost v hlavní větě: **won't start**. Po *until* přítomný čas *is*.

items.en: Will you call me when you know the result?
items.cz: Zavoláš mi, až budeš znát výsledek?
items.gap: ____ me when you know the result? (call)
accepts: Will you call me when you know the result?
items.wrong: Will you call me when you will know the result?
items.explanation: Future question: **Will you call**. And present simple *know* after *when*.
items.explanation_cz: Otázka o budoucnosti: **Will you call**. A po *when* přítomný čas *know*.

items.en: That bag looks heavy. I will carry it for you.
items.cz: Ta taška vypadá těžká. Ponesu ti ji.
items.gap: That bag looks heavy. I ____ it for you. (carry)
accepts: That bag looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.
That bag looks heavy. I will carry it for you.
items.wrong: That bag looks heavy. I will to carry it for you.
items.explanation: You see it now and offer now → **will carry**. Not a plan made before.
items.explanation_cz: Vidíš to teď a nabízíš teď → **will carry**. Ne plán z dřívějška.

items.en: I promise I won't tell anyone about it.
items.cz: Slibuju, že o tom nikomu neřeknu.
items.gap: I promise I ____ anyone about it. (not tell)
accepts: I promise I won't tell anyone about it.
I promise I will not tell anyone about it.
I promise that I won't tell anyone about it.
I promise that I will not tell anyone about it.
items.wrong: I promise I don't tell anyone about it.
items.explanation: A promise → **won't tell** (= will not). Bare present *don't tell* is a habit, not a promise.
items.explanation_cz: Slib → **won't tell** (= will not). Prostý přítomný *don't tell* je zvyk, ne slib.

items.en: It's cold in here. I will close the window.
items.cz: Je tu zima. Zavřu okno.
items.gap: It's cold in here. I ____ the window. (close)
accepts: It's cold in here. I'll close the window.
It's cold in here. I will close the window.
It is cold in here. I'll close the window.
It is cold in here. I will close the window.
items.wrong: It's cold in here. I close the window.
items.explanation: Cold now → decide now → **will close**. Not a plan.
items.explanation_cz: Zima teď → rozhodnutí teď → **will close**. Ne plán.

items.en: No problem. I will do it tomorrow.
items.cz: Žádný problém. Zítra to udělám.
items.gap: No problem. I ____ it tomorrow. (do)
accepts: No problem. I'll do it tomorrow.
No problem. I will do it tomorrow.
items.wrong: No problem. I do it tomorrow.
items.explanation: Deciding as you speak → **will do**. ~~I do it tomorrow~~ is the Czech calque.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhoduješ se při řeči → **will do**. ~~I do it tomorrow~~ je kalk z češtiny.

items.en: We don't have any milk. I will buy some on the way home.
items.cz: Nemáme mléko. Koupím nějaké cestou domů.
items.gap: We don't have any milk. I ____ some on the way home. (buy)
accepts: We don't have any milk. I'll buy some on the way home.
We don't have any milk. I will buy some on the way home.
We do not have any milk. I'll buy some on the way home.
We do not have any milk. I will buy some on the way home.
We have no milk. I'll buy some on the way home.
We have no milk. I will buy some on the way home.
items.wrong: We don't have any milk. I buy some on the way home.
items.explanation: You notice it now, you decide now → **will buy**.
items.explanation_cz: Všimneš si teď, rozhodneš se teď → **will buy**.

items.en: We are going to paint the kitchen this weekend. We bought the paint yesterday.
items.cz: O víkendu budeme malovat kuchyň. Tu barvu jsme koupili včera.
items.gap: We ____ the kitchen this weekend. We bought the paint yesterday. (paint)
accepts: We're going to paint the kitchen this weekend. We bought the paint yesterday.
We are going to paint the kitchen this weekend. We bought the paint yesterday.
items.wrong: We going to paint the kitchen this weekend. We bought the paint yesterday.
items.explanation: The paint is already bought — a plan made before → **are going to paint**.
items.explanation_cz: Barva už je koupená — plán z dřívějška → **are going to paint**.

items.en: Martina has decided. She is going to study in Vienna next year.
items.cz: Martina se rozhodla. Příští rok bude studovat ve Vídni.
items.gap: Martina has decided. She ____ in Vienna next year. (study)
accepts: Martina has decided. She's going to study in Vienna next year.
Martina has decided. She is going to study in Vienna next year.
items.wrong: Martina has decided. She going to study in Vienna next year.
items.explanation: *Has decided* → the plan exists → **is going to study**.
items.explanation_cz: *Has decided* → plán už existuje → **is going to study**.

items.en: Look at those black clouds. It is going to rain soon.
items.cz: Podívej na ty černé mraky. Brzy bude pršet.
items.gap: Look at those black clouds. It ____ soon. (rain)
accepts: Look at those black clouds. It's going to rain soon.
Look at those black clouds. It is going to rain soon.
items.wrong: Look at those black clouds. Soon will rain.
items.explanation: Evidence you can see → **is going to rain**. And English never drops the subject *it*.
items.explanation_cz: Důkaz, který vidíš → **is going to rain**. A angličtina nikdy nevynechá podmět *it*.

items.en: Be careful! You are going to break that glass.
items.cz: Opatrně! Rozbiješ tu sklenici.
items.gap: Be careful! You ____ that glass. (break)
accepts: Be careful! You're going to break that glass.
Be careful! You are going to break that glass.
items.wrong: Be careful! You going to break that glass.
items.explanation: About to happen, you can see it → **are going to break**. Don't lose the **are**.
items.explanation_cz: Hned se to stane, vidíš to → **are going to break**. Neztrať **are**.

items.en: They aren't going to sell the house this year. They've decided to wait.
items.cz: Letos ten dům prodávat nebudou. Rozhodli se počkat.
items.gap: They ____ the house this year. They've decided to wait. (not sell)
accepts: They aren't going to sell the house this year. They've decided to wait.
They are not going to sell the house this year. They've decided to wait.
They aren't going to sell the house this year. They have decided to wait.
They are not going to sell the house this year. They have decided to wait.
items.wrong: They are not going sell the house this year. They've decided to wait.
items.explanation: A decision already made, negative → **aren't going to sell**.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhodnutí už padlo, zápor → **aren't going to sell**.

items.en: I am playing tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
items.cz: V pátek večer hraju s Martinem tenis. Naplánovali jsme to včera.
items.gap: I ____ tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday. (play)
accepts: I'm playing tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
I am playing tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
I'm going to play tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
I am going to play tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
items.wrong: I am play tennis with Martin on Friday evening. We planned it yesterday.
items.explanation: Arranged with a person → **am playing**. Bare *play* would be a habit, not Friday's plan.
items.explanation_cz: Domluvené s někým → **am playing**. Prosté *play* by byl zvyk, ne páteční plán.

items.en: She is meeting the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
items.cz: Zítra v deset má schůzku s tím novým manažerem.
items.gap: She ____ the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow. (meet)
accepts: She's meeting the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
She is meeting the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
She has a meeting with the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
She's got a meeting with the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
She has got a meeting with the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
items.wrong: She is meet the new manager at ten o'clock tomorrow.
items.explanation: A fixed time in the diary → **is meeting**. *Meets* would be every day.
items.explanation_cz: Pevný čas v diáři → **is meeting**. *Meets* by bylo každý den.

items.en: We are flying to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
items.cz: V sobotu ráno letíme do Říma. Máme letenky.
items.gap: We ____ to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets. (fly)
accepts: We're flying to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
We are flying to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
We're going to fly to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
We are going to fly to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
items.wrong: We are fly to Rome on Saturday morning. We have the tickets.
items.explanation: Tickets bought, everything fixed → **are flying**.
items.explanation_cz: Letenky koupené, všechno pevné → **are flying**.

items.en: What time are you meeting Jana tomorrow?
items.cz: V kolik hodin se zítra sejdeš s Janou?
items.gap: What time ____ Jana tomorrow? (meet)
accepts: What time are you meeting Jana tomorrow?
items.wrong: What time you are meeting Jana tomorrow?
items.explanation: Question about an arrangement: **are you meeting**. *Do you meet* asks about a habit.
items.explanation_cz: Otázka na domluvu: **are you meeting**. *Do you meet* se ptá na zvyk.

items.en: Our train leaves at six forty tomorrow morning.
items.cz: Náš vlak zítra ráno odjíždí v šest čtyřicet.
items.gap: Our train ____ at six forty tomorrow morning. (leave)
accepts: Our train leaves at six forty tomorrow morning.
items.wrong: Our train is leave at six forty tomorrow morning.
items.explanation: A timetable → present simple: **leaves**, even for tomorrow.
items.explanation_cz: Jízdní řád → přítomný čas: **leaves**, i když jde o zítřek.

items.en: Are you going to accept their offer, or do you need more time?
items.cz: Přijmeš jejich nabídku, nebo potřebuješ víc času?
items.gap: ____ their offer, or do you need more time? (accept)
accepts: Are you going to accept their offer, or do you need more time?
Will you accept their offer, or do you need more time?
items.wrong: Are you going accept their offer, or do you need more time?
items.explanation: Asking about a plan → **Are you going to accept**. Keep the *to*.
items.explanation_cz: Ptáš se na plán → **Are you going to accept**. Nevynechej *to*.

items.en: I've decided. I am not going to wait for him any longer.
items.cz: Rozhodla jsem se. Už na něj nebudu čekat.
items.gap: I've decided. I ____ for him any longer. (not wait)
accepts: I've decided. I'm not going to wait for him any longer.
I have decided. I'm not going to wait for him any longer.
I've decided. I am not going to wait for him any longer.
I have decided. I am not going to wait for him any longer.
I've decided. I'm not going to wait for him anymore.
I've decided. I am not going to wait for him anymore.
I have decided. I'm not going to wait for him anymore.
I have decided. I am not going to wait for him anymore.
items.wrong: I've decided. I'm not going wait for him any longer.
items.explanation: *I've decided* → the decision exists → **am not going to wait**.
items.explanation_cz: *I've decided* → rozhodnutí už existuje → **am not going to wait**.

items.en: I think our team will win the match on Sunday.
items.cz: Myslím, že náš tým v neděli ten zápas vyhraje.
items.gap: I think our team ____ the match on Sunday. (win)
accepts: I think our team will win the match on Sunday.
I think our team'll win the match on Sunday.
I think that our team will win the match on Sunday.
items.wrong: I think our team will wins the match on Sunday.
items.explanation: An opinion (*I think*) → **will win**. And after *will*, the verb stays bare: no *-s*.
items.explanation_cz: Názor (*I think*) → **will win**. Po *will* zůstává sloveso holé: bez *-s*.

items.en: Look at the traffic. We are going to be late for the concert.
items.cz: Podívej na ten provoz. Přijdeme na koncert pozdě.
items.gap: Look at the traffic. We ____ late for the concert. (be)
accepts: Look at the traffic. We're going to be late for the concert.
Look at the traffic. We are going to be late for the concert.
items.wrong: Look at the traffic. We going to be late for the concert.
items.explanation: You can see the traffic now — evidence → **are going to be** late.
items.explanation_cz: Provoz vidíš teď — důkaz → **are going to be** late.

items.en: We won't book the hotel until you choose the week.
items.cz: Nezarezervujeme ten hotel, dokud nevybereš týden.
items.gap: We won't book the hotel until you ____ the week. (choose)
accepts: We won't book the hotel until you choose the week.
We will not book the hotel until you choose the week.
items.wrong: We won't book the hotel until you will choose the week.
items.explanation: After **until**: present simple — **choose**. The future already sits in *won't book*.
items.explanation_cz: Po **until**: přítomný čas — **choose**. Budoucnost už nese *won't book*.

items.en: We'll stay in the garden until it starts getting dark.
items.cz: Zůstaneme na zahradě, dokud se nezačne stmívat.
items.gap: We'll stay in the garden ____ it starts getting dark.
accepts: We'll stay in the garden until it starts getting dark.
We will stay in the garden until it starts getting dark.
items.wrong: We'll stay in the garden until it will start getting dark.
items.explanation: Czech *dokud se nezačne* → **until**, and present simple after it: it **starts**.
items.explanation_cz: České *dokud se nezačne* → **until**, a po něm přítomný čas: it **starts**.
